title: The youngest (1 Samuel 16)
hook: man sees the face, but the Lord beholdeth the heart; David is out with the sheep
carry: the lord looks at the heart

segments.voice: Yesterday, Saul, the tallest man in Israel, hiding in the baggage on the day he was chosen. Your line was hiding in the baggage. Where did you step out? Day four hundred.

Four hundred days on this path, and today is a day about being overlooked. Saul's reign has gone wrong, and God sends old Samuel to Bethlehem with a horn of oil, to the house of a man named Jesse, Isai in the Douay-Rheims. One of Jesse's sons will be the next king. Jesse lines them up. The oldest walks in first, Eliab, and he looks the part: tall, strong, the kind of man you'd cast as a king. Samuel takes one look and thinks, surely this is the one. After all, the last king was chosen standing head and shoulders above the crowd.
screen: `A HORN OF OIL TO BETHLEHEM.` → `JESSE LINES UP HIS SONS.` → `SURELY THIS IS THE ONE.`

segments.voice: And God stops him. In the Douay-Rheims: "Look not on his countenance, nor on the height of his stature." Then the line this whole chapter is built on: "man seeth those things that appear, but the Lord beholdeth the heart." Notice the dig at height. Yesterday the crowd cheered a king because he was tall. Today God says, don't measure that way. So the parade goes on. The second son, no. The third, no. Seven sons pass in front of Samuel, and to each one the answer is the same: the Lord hath not chosen this one. Samuel is puzzled. Are these all your sons? And Jesse says, almost as an afterthought: well, there's the youngest. He's out keeping the sheep. Nobody thought to call him in. A family gathering to meet a prophet, and the youngest boy is left in the fields with the animals. Samuel says: we won't sit down until he comes. They fetch him. And the text, honestly, says he was good-looking too, ruddy and handsome. God's choice isn't against beauty; it just isn't based on it. The Lord says: arise, anoint him, for this is he. Samuel pours the oil in the middle of his brothers, and the Spirit of the Lord comes upon David from that day on. This is a pattern the Bible loves: the younger brother, the overlooked one, the shepherd. Catholics see it run all the way to Bethlehem again, where the son of David is born among shepherds, and to Mary's song: he hath exalted the humble.
screen: `LOOK NOT ON HIS HEIGHT.` · `SEVEN SONS, AND NONE IS CHOSEN.` · `THE YOUNGEST, OUT WITH THE SHEEP.` · `ANOINTED AMONG HIS BROTHERS.` · then, large: `THE LORD BEHOLDETH THE HEART.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: see someone's heart today. Settle, and breathe. Think of someone you've quietly sized up by the outside. The coworker who talks too much. The relative who dresses oddly. The person at church you've decided you know. Picture them like the youngest out in the field: the one nobody thought to call in. Then ask what you might find if you looked at their heart. What are they carrying? What are they good at that nobody notices? If you pray, you can ask to see them the way God sees. The bell holds the time.
The youngest. David, Jesse's eighth son, left out in the fields with the sheep, and the one God chose because the Lord looks at the heart. Today's word.
Your line: the lord looks at the heart. Today, call in one person who usually gets left out, and listen to them. Day four hundred.

howItsDone: Catholics hear David's anointing at Mass, including on the Fourth Sunday of Lent in one year of the cycle, and the Church often points to it when speaking of how God chooses the humble and overlooked.

fork.setup: you're Samuel. seven of Jesse's sons have passed in front of you, and God has said no to every one. what do you do?
options: anoint the oldest anyway; he looks the part.
ask if there are any more sons.
go home and try another family.
fork.reveal: he asks, are here all thy sons? there's the youngest, out with the sheep. Samuel won't sit down until he comes, and anoints him among his brothers.

original.note: Hebrew: heart, the inner self where a person thinks, chooses and loves. The Lord looks on the heart.

trapdoor: what you thought: a nice saying about inner beauty.
what it means: right after Israel chose a king for his height, God tells Samuel not to measure that way, and picks the youngest, left out in the fields.
what a scholar hears: levav, heart, in Hebrew is the seat of thought and will, not just feeling. and the younger son chosen over the elder is a pattern across Genesis and beyond.

notes: David as Jesse's eighth son follows 1 Samuel 16:10–11 and 17:12; 1 Chronicles 2:15 lists him as the seventh. 'Seven sons pass' and 'eighth son' follow 1 Samuel; confirm.
1 Samuel 16:1b, 6–7, 10–13a is the first reading for the Fourth Sunday of Lent, Year A; confirm.
Hebrew in 16:7: confirm the form (lebab / levav) and pronunciation.
Mary's Magnificat line (Luke 1:52, 'he hath exalted the humble') is spoken as a paraphrase; confirm.
